text:
maya: quick sanity check — evening shoulder (EU) is spiking tokens/sec and we're hitting headroom on the small-slab pools. seeing sustained 16k tokens/s per-GPU for 30m windows. can we avoid a slab bump?

sam: do you have the breakdown by concurrent requests vs avg tokens/request?

maya: yup, threw a quick extract from the simulator:
```
period: 18:00-18:30 CET
concurrent_reqs_p50: 420
concurrent_reqs_p95: 1120
avg_tokens_per_req: 38
tokens_per_sec_observed: 15800
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.68
warmup_waste_ratio: 0.12
```

alex: that warmup_waste looks high for the shoulder. any recent model switches or quantization changes?

maya: we rolled a new q4 profile two nights ago to reduce cost. might be increasing cold-kv misses.

jon: note EU egress limits also cause some tail amplification — requests that get routed cross-region add 30-60ms and push queuing. combined effect reduces effective tokens/sec per GPU.

sam: rough calc — if kv hit went from 0.68 -> 0.78 we reclaim ~10% tokens/sec headroom, right?

alex: about that. basic model: effective_tokens = raw_tokens * (1 - warmup_waste) * (1 - cross_region_penalty) * kv_hit_rate_effect. hacky but useful for quick checks.

maya: i ran a short sim with the new q4 and higher cache TTL, command used:
```
./tools/headroom_sim --region eu-west --model q4_1x --concurrency-dist p50=420,p95=1120 --avg-tokens 38 --kv-hit 0.68 --warmup 0.12
```
output snippet:
```
sim_window: 30m
peak_effective_tokens_per_gpu: 15.8k
required_gpus_for_95p: 42
current_small_slab_gpus: 36
projected_shortfall: 6 gpus -> ~36 GPU-hours extra (30m spikes over evening)
```

jon: cost note — 36 GPU-hours in eu-west on our reserved plan = ~€540 (ballpark). Can we instead throttle best-effort routes or tighten canary percentage to save cost?

alex: we should try three mitigations in parallel: 1) bump prefix cache TTL to reduce warmup waste, 2) enable local-only routing for critical routes in eu-west for 1h window, 3) ephemeral slab burst (2-4 GPUs) for 1h from dedicated pool.

sam: local-only routing might increase queuing elsewhere; need to simulate fallback. i can run a headroom-sweep that includes routing policy change.

maya: agreed. also suggest adding a short-term A/B: 20% of traffic on q4 -> q8 variant to see tail impact. if quality ok, we can shift more and reduce GPU count.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: prefix-cache-ttl bump -> canary on eu-west, rollout window 18:05-18:20 CET. ci-job: CI-1429.

jon: assign action items?

maya: maya -> validate sim assumptions + produce finalized numbers by 17:30 CET.
sam -> run headroom-sweep with routing policy variants and post results (eta 45m).
alex -> prep ephemeral slab config and cost estimate for 1h burst.
jon -> check billing impact and reserved pool availability.

sam: noted, starting sweep now. ping if anyone wants intermediate logs. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maya: i'll watch infra-bot canary and flag rollback if error rate or tail-latency > 2x baseline.

alex: if we need quick short-term capacity, i can provision two fractional GPUs from the dedicated pool for 1h now. cheaper than full slab bump.

maya: perfect. thanks team, will post numbers in this thread. :thumbsup:
